newsitem.title: USA: US House keeps federal crop insurance for tobacco.
newsitem.headline: US House keeps federal crop insurance for tobacco.

text.p: The U.S. House echoed a Senate vote by refusing on Thursday to ban federally subsidized crop insurance for tobacco.
Representatives rejected the idea, 209-216. A similar proposal failed narrowly last year.
On Wednesday, the Senate rejected, 47-53, an amendment by Senator Dick Durbin, Illinois Democrat, to deny federal crop insurance and disaster payments to tobacco.
The votes in both chambers were part of work on fiscal 1998 agriculture appropriations bills.
"Let's not mince words. Tobacco kills," Representative Merrill Cook, Utah Republican, said in arguing there was no reason for the government to support tobacco growing, even indirectly.

Democrat Scotty Baesler from Kentucky, one of the top tobacco states, said the antitobacco activists were inconsistent despite their arguments that they wanted parallel health and crop subsidy policies. No one was ready to renounce the billions of dollars raised in excise taxes on tobacco, he said.
"Are we trying to cut that out" Baseler said. "Hyprocrisy! Hypocrisy is we want to take from the farmers and stick it to the farmer at the same time."
